indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the singer holds the relations within

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
kin are one's relations

explanation.surface: A cowboy crooner meets up while putting up members of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like amusing but means hosting, so one piece holds the other; 'Meet' as a verb fits the phrasal answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk into someone is to bump into or encounter them, a colloquial sense of meeting.

clue.text: Slip under front of truck in panic

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece placed under another follows it
the front of a word is its opening letter, here taken from truck

parts.note: a slip is a small mistake, an error

explanation.surface: Someone slips beneath the front of a lorry and is terrified.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is extreme fear, a near-synonym of panic as a noun.

indicators.note: not entirely tells us to drop the final letter of the synonym for stiff

parts.note: stiff means hard, rigid
a vest is an undergarment worn on the upper body in Britain

explanation.surface: Collect some underclothes that are only somewhat starched.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a VEST is an undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To harvest crops is to gather them in, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Wandering king managed to access help

indicators.note: to access means to get into, so the king and managed go inside help

parts.note: to abet is to help, usually in wrongdoing
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex
to run a business is to manage it, so managed gives ran

explanation.surface: A roving monarch manages to get assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wandering' is the definition, though the surface makes it describe the king; 'to access' means to get into.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant means straying from the normal course, as a wandering thing does.

indicators.note: ridiculously signals that the letters of the following words are absurdly rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wears an absurdly big frock without caring.
explanation.definitionFit: Regardless used as an adverb means in any case or anyway, the same as anyhow.

indicators.note: something bitten by a beak is held inside it, so one sits inside the bird

parts.note: a heron is a long-legged wading bird
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A horse is pecked by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is a slang term for the drug, not the animal the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is long-standing street slang for this opiate drug.

clue.text: Old man's port, a US city

parts.note: old man is slang for father, pa, with the possessive s
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: Dad's harbour turns out to be an American town.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasadena is a city in Los Angeles County, California, so an example of a US city.

indicators.note: in puts the victory abbreviation inside the shortened word
short tells us to cut the last letter off the synonym for race

parts.note: a breed is a race or strain of animals

explanation.surface: Someone notes a win in a brief running contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims BREED to BREE, and 'in' places V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a long musical note, worth two semibreves, so it is a kind of note.

definitions.meaning: to miss something out is to omit or pass over it
to trip along is to move lightly with hops, as children do

explanation.definitionFit: To skip is both to omit something and to hop lightly along, two separate verb senses.

parts.note: the clue is a four-letter word for good ... written backwards, so the answer describes the clue itself

explanation.walkthrough: The query mark invites the solver to describe what the clue is: a word for luck turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal of fortune is a sudden change of luck, and here also literally luck reversed.

parts.note: the clue is the word reply spelt backwards, a response written in reverse

explanation.walkthrough: Describe what the clue shows: a response read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer back is to give a cheeky retort, and the clue is literally a response going backwards.

annotationWithheld.why: Spelling withholding "C", cunning: WIT(C)H + CRAFT needs 'withholding' split as WITH (fodder) plus 'holding' (container indicator), one word doing two jobs, which the check refuses

definitions.meaning: upright, on one's feet rather than lying down

explanation.definitionFit: Standing means upright, and it also means one's status or reputation.

clue.text: Wave painted with energy, though little movement of water

indicators.note: to wave is to move back and forth, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A painted wave full of energy hardly shows the sea moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' sounds like the sea but is the anagram signal, shuffling PAINTED plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: Neap tides are those with the smallest range between high and low water, so little tidal movement.

clue.text: One doesn't believe two articles at first

parts.note: a is the indefinite article in English
the is the definite article in English
first is abbreviated 1st, with the figure one written as the letter I

explanation.surface: A sceptic objects to a pair of articles from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 in 1ST is read as the letter I; 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist is a person who does not believe in any god.

parts.note: in a down clue these letters spell a woodland plant reading upwards

explanation.walkthrough: In the grid the word reads from bottom to top, so a kind of tree goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: To spruce up is to smarten, and here a tree (spruce) literally goes up the grid.

clue.text: God housed in conurbation seeks unimpeded view

indicators.note: housed in means placed inside, so the god goes inside the conurbation

parts.note: a city is a large urban area, a conurbation
a lar is a Roman household god, one of the Lares

explanation.surface: A deity living in a big town wants a clear outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: LAR is the singular of Lares, Roman household gods, an old crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarity is clearness, the quality of seeing without obstruction.

clue.text: Postpone dance after some weeks, name withdrawn

indicators.note: after places the dance at the end
withdrawn means taken away, so the name letter is removed

parts.note: a month is a span of some weeks
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone delays a dance by several weeks and takes their name off the list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' takes N out of MONTH, leaving MOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To mothball a plan is to shelve it for later, an idiom for postponing.

clue.text: Essential to stop a question appearing dull

indicators.note: Essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Interrupting a question is vital if it seems boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means not transparent or lustrous, so dull in appearance.

definitions.meaning: as in a last ..., the final option
a place people go for holidays, such as a seaside town

explanation.definitionFit: Resort means both a recourse turned to (last resort) and a holiday spot.

parts.note: in a down clue these letters spell a word for moist reading upwards

explanation.walkthrough: In the grid the word reads from bottom to top, so moisture climbs. RISING DAMP is a common British building problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising damp is moisture climbing walls from the ground, and here wetness literally climbs the grid.

parts.note: the letters spell a word for a levy written backwards

explanation.walkthrough: Duty is a tax, and here it comes back in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tax returns are forms declaring income, and here a levy literally returns backwards.

clue.text: Bowled, needing edge — and getting one!

definitions.text: Bowled, needing edge — and getting one!

parts.note: B is the cricket scoring abbreviation for bowled
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A batsman is bowled when he needed to nick it, and finds the edge after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: B plus a rim gives an edge, so the clue 'gets one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brim is the edge of a cup or hat, so the answer is itself an edge.

clue.text: Fellow in nude unfortunately short of a nibble

indicators.note: in places the fellow letter inside the rearranged word
unfortunately signals that the word nude ends up in a bad, disordered state

explanation.surface: A naked man is unluckily left without a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges NUDE to UNED, and 'in' puts F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfed means not given food, so lacking even a small bite.

clue.text: Problem in The Listener can fool us

parts.note: a tin is a can
a nit is a fool, a nitwit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trouble in the famous crossword magazine could make fools of us.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famous British crossword series, but here 'The Listener' just means one who hears.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinnitus is ringing in the ears, a problem for anyone who listens.
